page: Microsoft Azure E32-8ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the EDSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel Xeon 8370C cores operating at 2.8 GHz. The server is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 32.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with a 1229 GB local solid-state drive (SSD), and the system lacks dedicated GPU hardware. The x86_64 CPU architecture supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and cryptographic acceleration via VAES and SHA_NI.

Benchmark evaluations place the E32-8ds_v5 in the average performance tier across most compute and memory metrics. The system achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1681.0 and a multi-core score of 6221.0, alongside a Passmark CPU score of 11487.3. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only cached small-block bandwidth of 417.04 GB/sec, which drops to 59.66 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Database and web serving capabilities are demonstrated by a Passmark database operations score of 4096.32, Redis SET performance of 7.97 million operations per second, and a static web serving throughput of 12.28 GB/sec.

The server exhibits clear performance tradeoffs, particularly in machine learning workloads. While LLM inference with a small 135M parameter model is functional at 174.99 tokens per second for text generation, performance drops significantly to a weak 7.57 tokens per second with a medium 7B model, and large 70B models are unsupported due to the lack of GPU acceleration. Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio and the presence of local SSD storage, this configuration is highly cost-efficient for memory-intensive, non-GPU workloads. It is best suited for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, data warehousing, and enterprise applications requiring substantial memory capacity without high parallel compute demands.
